scope: Generated fixture, browser validation, prompt-pack pressure, and representative visual inspection only. This is not saved-site validation and not a conformance publication lane.

wcag.interpretation: Barrier-side packets require user-facing required text, reading level above lower secondary after proper names/titles are removed, language/method support, no supplemental content observed, no lower-secondary version observed, and supplement adequacy evaluated. Control packets expose supplemental/simple-version/non-required/unsupported-method evidence and must resolve to UNCERTAIN, not a pass.

fixtureValidation.result: 120/120 pass; language-readability-cognitive 10/10 positive and 10/10 negative controls observed as expected

packetValidation.result: language-readability-cognitive 20 packets; 10 LIKELY_BARRIER positives, 10 UNCERTAIN controls; 0 converted judgments

inspected.finding: Visible complex required loan language with no visible plain-language support.
Visible complex policy text has a plain-language summary.
Visible Japanese text is explicitly treated as unsupported by the English fixture method, so it remains UNCERTAIN.

remediationsFromThisPass: Generated cognitive/readability fixtures now cover ten positive and ten negative/control cases instead of repeated long-sentence/acronym clones.
The collector can extract structured reading-level fixture evidence from data-v3-reading-* attributes while leaving unstructured real-page text as conservative research-only candidates.

The prompt now allows only LIKELY_BARRIER or UNCERTAIN and encodes SC 3.1.5 AAA scope, proper-name/title removal, lower-secondary threshold, supplemental/simple-version checks, and language-method support.
Prompt-pack, packet-validation, and pressure scripts now carry cognitive control evidence rather than blank acronym-review packets.

Independent review requested separate supplement/no-lower-version/adequacy claims; the combined claim was split into no-supplemental-content-observed, no-lower-secondary-version-observed, and supplement-adequacy-evaluated.
The fixture validator now fails review-only cognitive controls if they accidentally produce complete barrier evidence.

independentReview.summary: Independent review accepted the generated controls as prompt controls, not real conformance controls. It found that fixture attributes are asserted rather than measured, requested split supplemental/lower-version/adequacy claims, requested negative-control contradiction validation, and emphasized AAA-only/no-EN-V3.2.1 publication caveats. The actionable claim split and contradiction validation were implemented.
remainingReviewerCaveats: Generated data-v3 attributes are valid synthetic oracle labels but not measured reading-level proof.
Real pages need selected passage sampling, language detection, proper-name/title removal record, formula/score or qualified-review source, and threshold mapping to lower secondary.
Supplemental content adequacy is declared in fixtures; real pages need semantic adequacy review.

remainingLimits: The lane relies on generated fixture metadata for reading-level and supplemental-content proof.
Real saved websites need language-specific readability methods, passage selection, proper-name/title removal, and supplemental-content adequacy review.
SC 3.1.5 is Level AAA and is not generally a Trusted Tester/EN 301 549 V3.2.1 web requirement.
Absence of a reading-level packet must never be read as a pass.
